Mike B.: Heads up — after the q4b bringup on rm-7b I see a divergence in long-run traces around token ~32k. Not classic wrap; looks like a rotary-phase shear when cached KV index grows past ~65k. Repro attached.

Anya L.: can you paste the minimal repro and the exact command you ran?

Mike B.:
```
# repro (short)
python tests/longctx_check.py --model rm-7b-q4b --seed 42 --max_tokens 120000 --batch 1
# observed
ERROR: kv_index_mismatch step=32012 prefix_hash=0x7f2a
trace: decode_mismatch at pos=32011
```

Samir: hmm, that pattern screams per-layer rotary scale mismatch after quant folding. Try toggling ROTARY_SCALE (0.999 vs 1.001) or forcing ROTARY_BASE override. Also try --cache-shards=1 to rule out sharding reindex.

Mike B.: quick smoke results: ROTARY_SCALE=0.999 survived 50k tokens in my run, 1.001 failed faster (repro at ~32k). Posting the tiny token-diff around failure:
```
--- expected (cpu fp64)
+++ observed (quant runner)
@@
- " the meeting ended with a summary ."
+ " the meeting ended with an summary ."
```

Natalie C.: I reproduced on int4v2 on rtx-a100. latency stable but decoder drift appears as off-by-one in positions after cache hits increase. My hypothesis: some quant kernel inlines a scale into rotary math, and when we rehydrate KV across shards the per-layer scale/offset isn't re-applied consistently.

Mike B.: good note. I can try a per-layer dump of rotary multipliers and compare kernel outputs vs reference.

ci-bot: CI job queued: longctx-phase-shear-1753214567 (hw=dedi-rtx2) — https://ci.redwood/tests/1753214567 :robot_face:

Anya L.: I'll bisect layers next (run with --max_rope_layer=24 then 25 etc). Queuing on dedicated-rtx2 now and assigning to @Mike B. :eyes:

Samir: if bisect narrows it to a layer range we can try a hotfix: reapply explicit rotary scaling post-quant-fold for those layers and run lightweight evals.

Mike B.: sounds good. I'll own follow-up and post logs. Thanks everyone.
